summary: Validation passed (all six deterministic checks) and the rendered artifact is now tightly cropped: the PDF page is 356.7x138.7 pt (aspect 2.57) and reconstruction.png contains only the dashed-box drawing, with the target's aspect ~2.70 - iteration-1's 'uncropped US-Letter page' finding is resolved. Also resolved: the +/-/v column is on one x (7.5 cm = 0.62 of the width, target 0.629), the GFM/grid divider is at 0.694 (target 0.706), the source at 0.917 (target 0.924), the 'grid' caption at 0.849 (target ~0.848), and the topology/arrow direction/polarity and the symbol inventory (rectangle+diagonal block, L, R, generic, sV, dashed groups) all match. The iteration-1 instruction to make Z_g straddle the divider is contradicted by the target: in reference/target.png the Z_g body lies wholly inside the 'grid' box (~0.77-0.86 of the drawing width) and the divider crosses bare wire, so the current layout draws the group boundary through the Z_g symbol and through its label and reverses the two bare-wire runs. Remaining items are geometry/polish (inductor coil, converter-block proportions, vertical proportions, v_g label height, GFM caption offset). No human feedback was supplied, so there is nothing to address there. One more automatic iteration can close every item listed.

findings.description: Z_g is split by the GFM/grid divider: the grid-impedance body straddles the group boundary so part of a grid element is drawn inside the GFM group, and the two bare-wire runs between the port marks and the source are reversed relative to the target.
findings.evidence: Source: `z1=(8.05,3)`, `z2=(9.0,3)` with `to[generic]`; the GFM box ends at x=8.35 and the grid box starts at 8.45, so the divider (0.694 of the 12.1 cm width) crosses the 1.0 cm body at its 30% point. In current/reconstruction.png the dashed divider visibly cuts through the left third of the Z_g rectangle (body occupies ~0.665-0.744 W). In reference/target.png the divider (~0.70 W) crosses only bare wire; the Z_g rectangle sits wholly inside the 'grid' box at ~0.77-0.86 W with ~0.06 W of white space on either side. Consequence in the wire lengths (fraction of drawing width): port marks -> Z_g 0.045 W in the recon vs 0.134 W in the target; Z_g -> source 0.176 W vs 0.068 W.

findings.description: The 'Z_g' label is crossed by the group divider - both dashed edge lines run through the glyphs - and it is set higher than the L_f/R_f labels, pressed up toward the top dashed border. In the target all three component labels sit on one row, clear of the divider and the border.
findings.evidence: The label is auto-placed at the generic's midpoint x = 8.525 cm = 0.70 W, so both the GFM right edge (8.35) and the grid left edge (8.45) pass through the ~0.5 cm wide glyph block; this is plainly visible in current/reconstruction.png as dashes running through 'Z_g' at the top of the frame. Its row is visibly higher than the L_f/R_f labels (glyph tops reach the top dashed border at y=3.65). In reference/target.png the 'Z_g' label is at ~0.79-0.83 W on the same row as L_f (~0.36 W) and R_f (~0.51 W), with clear white space to the divider (~0.06 W) and to the top border (~0.045 H).

findings.description: The filter/arrow cluster is shifted ~0.04-0.05 of the width to the left of the target, which opens a bare-wire gap between R_f and the current arrow and squeezes the run from the port marks to Z_g; the current arrowhead is also far lighter than the target's solid triangle.
findings.evidence: Fractions of drawing width, target -> recon: L_f 0.324-0.433 -> 0.289-0.380; R_f 0.468-0.548 -> 0.417-0.479; arrow 0.577-0.623 -> 0.545-0.587; 'i' 0.597 -> 0.566. Gap R_f->arrow tail: 0.029 W in the target vs 0.066 W in the render; gap arrow head->'+': 0.006 W vs 0.033 W. In reference/target.png the R_f zigzag ends almost immediately before the arrow tail, whereas current/reconstruction.png shows a ~0.07 W bare segment. The target arrowhead is a filled triangle about 0.017 W long; the render's Stealth tip is roughly half that and barely visible at plot scale.

findings.description: L_f is drawn as a small, flat multi-loop coil instead of the target's large four-loop coil, so the inductor reads as visually subordinate to R_f, whereas in the target the coil is as tall as the resistor.
findings.evidence: In reference/target.png the coil spans ~0.109 W with four wide loops and a height (~0.07 H, about 22 px of the 297 px drawing height) comparable to the R_f zigzag amplitude. In current/reconstruction.png the coil spans ~0.09 W, is only ~0.03 H tall and shows 5-6 tight loops - visibly flatter and smaller than the adjacent resistor. Source: `\ctikzset{inductor=cute}` applied to `to[L, l=$L_f$]` across 3.5-4.6 cm.

findings.description: The converter block is a 2.5 x 3.0 portrait rectangle (50-degree diagonal) whereas the target block is essentially square (~185 x 182 px, ~45-degree diagonal); in the target the block's top edge stands above the upper wire, while the reconstruction puts the block's top and bottom edges exactly on the two wires.
findings.evidence: Source: `\draw (0.5,0) rectangle (3.0,3);` = 0.207 W x 0.682 H with a 3/2.5 diagonal. reference/target.png: block spans ~0.043-0.255 W horizontally and ~0.168-0.781 H vertically (185 x 182 px, i.e. square); its bottom edge lies on the return wire (~0.78 H) but its top edge is at ~0.168 H while the upper wire is at ~0.26 H, i.e. ~0.09 H above the wire, so the wire leaves the right edge below the top-right corner and the diagonal is ~45 degrees, not 50.

findings.description: The two horizontal wires are farther apart relative to the dashed boxes than in the target: the loop fills 0.68 of the box height instead of 0.52, and the headroom above the upper wire (0.65 cm) is roughly half the target's, which is why the component labels crowd the top border.
findings.evidence: Source: wires at y=0 and y=3, boxes y=-0.75..3.65 -> loop 3/4.4 = 0.682, top margin 0.65/4.4 = 0.148, bottom 0.75/4.4 = 0.170. reference/target.png: dashed boxes span ~0.06-0.95 of the image height with the wires at ~0.26 and ~0.78 of the drawing height -> loop 0.522, top margin 0.259, bottom 0.219. With the width kept at 12.1 cm this implies a drawing height of ~4.1-4.2 cm with the wires ~2.2 cm apart.

findings.description: The 'v_g' label sits above the source's mid-height, and the source centre is slightly high in the box; in the target the label is level with the circle centre, immediately to its left.
findings.evidence: Source: `\node[anchor=east] at (10.65,1.75) {$v_g$}` with the sV between y=1 and y=2 (centre 1.5), i.e. the label is 0.25 cm above the circle centre; the circle centre is at 0.489 of the box height (target ~0.545). In current/reconstruction.png 'v_g' reads above-left of the circle, whereas in reference/target.png it is beside the circle at its mid-height (y ~0.545 H, x ~0.83 W, circle centre ~0.92 W).

findings.description: The 'GFM converter' caption is centred under its box (0.345 W) but the target places it about 0.07 of the width further right (~0.42 W).
findings.evidence: Source: `\node at (4.175,-0.38) {GFM converter};` -> 4.175/12.1 = 0.345 W while the GFM box spans 0.0-0.690 W (centre 0.345 W). In reference/target.png the caption spans ~0.31-0.53 W (centre ~0.418 W) against a box spanning ~0.04-0.70 W (centre ~0.37 W), i.e. the target caption is right of the box centre. The 'grid' caption already matches (0.849 vs target ~0.848) and should not move.

nextActions: Move Z_g fully into the grid box: set z1=(9.30,3) and z2=(10.35,3) (0.77-0.856 of the 12.1 cm width, body ~1.05 cm), leaving the GFM box ending at 8.35 and the grid box starting at 8.45 so the divider crosses only bare wire as in the target; keep +/v/- near x=7.6 and the source near x=11.1-11.15 so the bare runs become ~1.6 cm (port marks -> Z_g) and ~0.75 cm (Z_g -> source).

Place the 'Z_g' label explicitly at the body centre (about (9.82,3.35)) so it sits on the same row as the L_f/R_f labels, and give it at least 0.15 cm clearance below the top dashed border (or raise the top border to y=3.8); then verify in the re-rendered PNG that no dashes touch any glyph.

Shift the filter cluster to the target fractions: L_f 3.9-5.2 cm, R_f 5.65-6.6 cm, current arrow 6.95-7.5 cm with 'i' at ~7.2 cm (keep +/v/- at 7.6 cm and the divider at 8.4 cm), and draw the arrowhead as a filled triangle of roughly the target's size (e.g. `>=triangle 45` or `-{Triangle}` with an enlarged tip).

Enlarge the inductor to the target's four-loop coil (e.g. `\ctikzset{inductor=american}` instead of `cute`, or raise `bipoles/cute inductor/height` and `.../width`) so that it is ~0.11 of the drawing width and roughly as tall as the R_f zigzag.

Make the converter block about 2.5 x 2.5 cm (square, ~45-degree diagonal) with its bottom edge on the return wire and its top edge ~0.3 cm above the upper wire, as in the target where the wire leaves the right edge below the top-right corner; keep DC upper-left (~28%/23%) and AC lower-right (~74%/87%).

Rescale the vertical layout toward the target's proportions, e.g. with the width fixed at 12.1 cm: lower wire y=0, upper wire y=2.2, top dashed border y=3.25, bottom border y=-0.9 (drawing ~12.1 x 4.15, aspect ~2.9, rendered page aspect ~2.74 vs the target's 2.70); move the sV to ~0.5-1.5, keep the source centre near the mid-height of the loop, and adjust the two captions to y~-0.5.
Lower the 'v_g' label to the source's mid-height (anchor=east at the circle centre y) so it reads beside the circle as in the target rather than above it.

Move the 'GFM converter' caption to ~x=5.0 cm (0.42 of the width) under its box, leave 'grid' at 10.275, then re-render and re-check, against the target fractions, that Z_g, the divider, the label row and the two bare-wire runs now match before yielding.
